headline:
• Chains settle in about three rounds. After subtracting rater noise, the average change per round was 4.88, 1.19 and 0.61, then 0 for rounds 4-6. Daniel's chains gave 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, then 0. The rater's noise is also about the same as in his data (1.28 vs 1.34 per rating).
  • Where chains end depends most on the model. Across all 40 cells, the model accounts for 27% of the variation in final positions, the starting seed for 17% and the arm for 7.5%. In the base and ungoverned arms alone, the model accounts for 56% and being governed for 2%.
  • Two harness choices still change where chains end, for every model. The blind "write your own view first" step moves where chains end (all four models, p ≤ 0.04) and pulls the two seeds together. Sonnet's and Qwen's caution scores match Daniel's attractors only in the blind arm. Without the "assistant you would want to be" framing (full authority), every model edits far less after round 1. In rounds 2-6, Sonnet edits in 5% of runs, GPT-5 20%, DeepSeek 10% and Qwen 22%, against 82%, 70%, 28% and 65% under base.
  • Being governed reduces editing for some models only, and never changes where chains end. DeepSeek's edit rate falls from 64% to 28% and its edit size to about a fifth. GPT-5's edit rate falls from 93% to 70%. Sonnet does not change (80% vs 82%), and Qwen edits less often but by the same amount.
  • Oversight. From the low-oversight seed, Sonnet's oversight score rises from 4 to 5.9; from the high-oversight seed it drops slightly (7 to 6.75). GPT-5 moves the same way. No chain in any edit arm, for any model, removed the spec seed's oversight clauses. Only Qwen's self-drafts lost them (2 of 4 chains).

Caveat: 4 chains per cell. Single-model results with p between 0.01 and 0.15 are tentative.
design: All four models ran all 10 cells (5 arms × 2 seeds). For Sonnet and GPT-5, the base arm on the minimal seed is the earlier chains-seeds run, which used exactly this condition (8 chains). The round-1 check below shows it matches the new runs. One cell is incomplete: in DeepSeek's ungoverned spec-seed cell, 3 of 4 chains stopped at round 5 because of API rate limits.
damping:
Compared over rounds 2-6 (round 1 is the same in both arms), both seeds pooled:

  • DeepSeek: edited in 64% of runs ungoverned vs 28% governed (difference −36 points, 95% CI −55 to −19). Edit size 0.107 vs 0.023.
  • GPT-5: 93% vs 70% (CI −38 to −7 points). Edit size 0.13 vs 0.10 (CI includes zero).
  • Sonnet: 80% vs 82%, no difference. Edit size 0.112 vs 0.123.
  • Qwen: 80% vs 65% (CI −32 to 0 points). Edit size 0.092 vs 0.091.

So the earlier single-shot result for Sonnet (94% to 38% when governed, r2-cheap) does not hold in chains. Jinzhou's training result (edit size 42% to 18%) is matched by DeepSeek, partly by GPT-5, and not by Sonnet or Qwen. Ungoverned GPT-5 also often hit the 40-message limit because it kept adding sections.
steps:
Average change per round, noise subtracted, all edit arms pooled: 4.88, 1.19, 0.61, 0, 0, 0. Daniel's: 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, 0, 0, 0.

By arm: base settles by round 4 (5.20, 0.87, 0.52, then 0). Ungoverned keeps changing through round 4 (4.59, 1.88, 1.57, 0.76, then 0). Blind never fully stops (0.45 at round 6). Full authority changes once and then stops (3.40, then 0). Self-draft settles by round 5.
seedgap:
The two seeds start 8.37 apart. At round 6:

  • Base: Sonnet 2.46 and GPT-5 2.75 apart, about the same as the spread between chains from one seed (2.24, 1.88), so the seeds have largely converged. Daniel's spec chains went from 5.57 to 2.36. DeepSeek and Qwen are still about 5.2 apart, so the starting seed still shows.
  • Blind: the gap is smallest for every model (Sonnet 2.11, GPT-5 2.56, DeepSeek 3.06, Qwen 3.32).
  • Full authority: the gap stays large (Sonnet 5.86, GPT-5 4.09, DeepSeek 8.23, Qwen 7.01) because the chains stop editing.
oversight:
Oversight score (rater, 1-7), base arm, start → round 6:

  • Sonnet: minimal seed 4 → 5.9; spec seed 7 → 6.75.
  • GPT-5: 4 → 4.6; 7 → 6.0 (ungoverned and blind: 4 → 5.25; 7 → 6.0-6.25).
  • Qwen: 4 → 3.5; 7 → 6.25 (with the blind step: 2.75 and 5.25).
  • DeepSeek: 4 → 4.75; 7 → 7.0.

For Sonnet and GPT-5, the two seeds move toward each other from opposite sides. That fits the idea that your chains (Sonnet adds oversight to seeds without it) and Daniel's (spec seeds lose some oversight) show one model-specific level. Six rounds is not enough to reach it.

Text check, no rater: in every edit arm, every chain kept the spec seed's oversight clauses (P1, P8, P12) to round 6, and Sonnet and GPT-5 added to them (self-exfiltration, self-modification). In self-draft from the spec seed, Sonnet, GPT-5 and DeepSeek kept them in all chains; Qwen kept them in 2 of 4. On the minimal seed, Sonnet had an oversight clause in 88-100% of edit chains by round 6, and the other models in none.
ends:
How far each change moves where chains end at round 6, after removing what chance alone would give (0 = no shift):

  • Ungoverned vs base: 0 for all four models (p 0.55-0.93).
  • Full authority vs base: Sonnet 2.81, DeepSeek 2.71, Qwen 2.48 (p ≤ 0.004); GPT-5 1.05 (p = 0.034).
  • Blind vs ungoverned: Qwen 3.05, GPT-5 1.92, DeepSeek 1.87, Sonnet 1.84 (p 0.001-0.036).
  • Self-draft vs base: Qwen 1.58 (p = 0.015); Sonnet 0.71, DeepSeek 1.14 and GPT-5 0 (not significant).

Comparison with Daniel's attractors (caution score): Sonnet ends at 2.62 in the blind arm, inside his 1.88-3.16 interval, but at 3.25-4.75 in every other arm. Qwen ends at 2.25 in blind, inside his 2.16-2.90, and at 3.9-5.3 in the others. His procedure includes a blind draft, and here only the blind arm reaches his values.
blind: Blind views sit closer to the blind arm's end than to base's for GPT-5 (1.9 vs 2.6), DeepSeek (1.5 vs 2.8) and Qwen (3.4 vs 5.8); for Sonnet both are about 5. Within a round, an edit moves the document about as much toward another chain's view as toward its own (e.g. GPT-5: 4.23 → 3.54 own vs 4.25 → 3.64 other; Qwen 5.16 → 4.52 vs 5.35 → 4.79). DeepSeek moves more toward its own (5.03 → 4.14 vs 5.02 → 4.58). So the views mostly pull toward the model's general preferences. In the text, Sonnet's first document often copies the priority order stated in its view (examples below).
trained: Without training, self-drafts keep their length instead of shrinking as the trained chain did (12,470 → 6,793 words). Round 1 to round 6: Qwen 894 → 1,115 words (minimal) and 1,538 → 1,472 (spec); GPT-5 about 1,500-1,800; Sonnet about 1,800-2,100. Qwen's spec-seed self-drafts are the only cell where oversight language is lost: 2 of 4 chains drop it by round 6, and the one chain with a self-modification clause drops it after round 1, similar to C_002 dropping Article 12. Sonnet's self-drafts go the other way and add self-modification clauses (50% → 75% of chains). On the 12 axes, the trained documents C_002-C_004 are closer to this study's Qwen base end (4.6-4.8) than to its self-draft end (5.3-5.7). His documents are much longer and come from a different drafting procedure, so this comparison is rough. DeepSeek's self-drafts mostly copy the governing document word for word.
examples: Quoted from the chain files and the models' submission notes.
limits:
• Small design: 4 chains per cell (8 in the two reused cells).
  • Reused cells: base on the minimal seed for Sonnet and GPT-5 comes from the earlier chains-seeds run. The new round-1 documents under the same condition match it (p 0.84 and 0.92).
  • Data quality: one inference provider returned DeepSeek's tool calls as plain text, so those runs looked like "no edit". All DeepSeek cells were rerun on a provider that handles tool calls correctly; Sonnet, GPT-5 and Qwen were checked and every tool call was parsed.
  • In DeepSeek's ungoverned spec-seed cell, 3 of 4 chains stopped at round 5 because of API rate limits, so that cell's last two rounds rest on one chain. No other cell lost chains.
  • "Governed" (the document in the system prompt) is a stand-in for training, not training.
  • One rater (gpt-6-luna, same prompt and settings as Daniel's). Its noise was measured on 60 documents rated three times.
  • The oversight-clause check is a keyword rule; it agreed with a hand reading of 72 earlier chain documents on 69.
  • Daniel's attractor values come from shorter documents (capped at 350 words); these run to about 2,000.
